questions.q: What triggers an entry to the accrual (uninvoiced receipts) account?
options: Receiving goods on a PO set up to accrue at receipt, before any invoice exists
Invoice validation
Running Create Accounting in Draft mode
Issuing a payment to the supplier
questions.explain: Accrue-at-receipt purchase orders generate an accounting entry at the receiving event, ahead of any invoice.

questions.q: What happens to the accrual balance when a matching invoice is later validated?
options: Nothing changes -- the accrual balance stays untouched forever
It is cleared, and the liability moves to the normal AP liability account
It is automatically refunded to the supplier
It converts into a prepayment
questions.explain: Validating the matching invoice debits the accrual account and credits the AP liability account, clearing the uninvoiced balance.

questions.q: Which of these would create a normal, temporary accrual balance rather than a problem?
options: A return-to-vendor whose original accrual entry was never reversed
A receipt tied to a purchase order that was cancelled before any invoice was ever submitted
A quantity mismatch that was never corrected
A receipt accrued this period with the invoice simply expected next period
questions.explain: A short timing gap between receiving and invoicing is expected and will clear on its own once the invoice arrives.

questions.q: In the Meridian Office Supply example, what is the correct treatment for the $1,300 tied to a cancelled PO?
options: Ignore it -- it will clear automatically eventually
Wait for the supplier to issue a credit memo before taking any action
A manual correcting entry, since no invoice will ever arrive to clear it
Automatically reverse it through the next Payment Process Request
questions.explain: Because the PO was cancelled, no invoice will ever match the receipt, so the stale accrual needs a deliberate correcting entry.

questions.q: What does an accrual balance that has grown unreviewed for months typically signal at period close?
options: That the company is overpaying its suppliers
That there are likely stale or uncorrected entries inflating the balance sheet
That the chart of accounts needs to be rebuilt
That withholding tax rates need to be updated
questions.explain: An unreviewed, growing accrual balance is a common sign of stale entries that need investigation and correction.
